_meta.preparation_standard: Hand-drafted in-chat (Opus 4.8). Answers the printed gem 'How is Jehovah the Great Potter?' (Jer 18:6; 19:10, 11). Gemini-3.5-flash audience critic: flawless.

notes.content: What struck me reading these two chapters back to back is how the pottery picture changes between them. In Jeremiah 18:6 the clay is still on the wheel — soft, workable — and Jehovah says, "as the clay in the hand of the potter, so are you in my hand." If the vessel gets marred, the potter doesn't throw the clay out. He works it back down and remakes it into another vessel. That's mercy — as long as the clay stays soft, he can reshape it. But then in chapter 19, it's a different picture. Now it's a flask — already fired, already hardened — and Jehovah tells Jeremiah to break it, "so that it can never be repaired." Same clay, same potter. The only thing that changed is whether it was still soft or already set. And that's the part that stayed with me — the potter didn't harden that flask. The fire of the nation's own rebellion did. So it never left me wondering whether Jehovah could reshape me. Chapter 18 already answered that. It left me wondering whether I'm staying soft enough to let him.
